bādhana:
1bādhana
n. [from bādheti1], catching, trapping; snaring; S V 148,.18 (luddā makkaṭavīthīsu lepaṃ oḍḍenti makkaṭānaṃ ~āya); Ja I 211,6* (na maṃ jālasmiṃ ~aṃ; 211,12´ : yaṃ pi me jālasmiṃ ~aṃ ahosi taṃ pi maṃ na bādhesī ti).

2bādhana
n., ~ā, f. [from bādheti2; ts], oppressing, afflicting, hurting; discomfort; Vism 495,.34 (°-lakkhaṇaṃ dukkhasaccaṃ); Pv-a 116,.23 (tassa vā pubbakārino ~ena hato); Vibh-a 75,.8 (heṭhanā ti pāṇippahārādīhi ~ā dukkhuppādanā); Sadd 446,.8 (kilisa ~e); — bādhana- iic in Ee at Spk III 134,.25 is prob. wr; Be, Ce, Se, Paṭis-a 689,.16 dhāvana-; —    abādhana, n., not hurting, not oppressing; Th-a III 24,.23 (aññamaññaṃ ~ena).
cittaka:
1cittaka
m. [S. citraka], a plant; SAF: leadwort, Plumbago indica L.; Abh 580 (~o tv aggisaññito); Samantak 736 (°-japā).

2cittaka
n. [S. lex. citraka], an ornamental mark; an ornamental or sectarian mark on the forehead; Abh 300 (tilako … ~aṃ); Sp 1293,.17 (hatthaṃ koṭṭāpentī ti agga-bāhaṃ koṭṭāpetvā morapattādīhi ~aṃ karonti, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be cittālaṅkāraṃ); —      °-dharakumma,   m., a kind of land turtle or tortoise (with a marking like a tilaka? ); Mil 408,.13 (~o udakabhayā udakaṃ parivajjetvā vicarati); — see also cittatilaka (sv citta2).

cittakā
(and cittikā1), f. cittaka m. (and n.?) [from citta2], a many-coloured woollen covering; Abh 312 (uṇṇāmayaṃ tv attharaṇaṃ ~ā vānacittakaṃ, Ce so; Be ~aṃ); Vin I 192,.15 (… goṇako ~ā paṭikā paṭalikā …, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se ~o; Sp 1086,.6 : ~o ti vānacitro uṇṇā-mayattharaṇo, Ce so; Be ~ā ti; Ee, Se ~o ti vāḷacitta-uṇṇāmayattharako, prob. wr) ≠ II 169,.33 (Ee, Se ~ā; Be, Ce ~o) ≠ A I 181,.21 (Ce, Ee ~ā; Be ~o; Se cittikā; Mp II 292,.30 : ~o ti vānacittaṃ uṇṇāmayattharaṇaṃ, Be so; Ce, Ee cittikā ti; Se ~o ti ratanavicitra-uṇṇāmayattharaṇaṃ); Ap 314,.11 (tūlikā vikatikāyo kaṭṭhissā ~ā bahū … labhāmi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee cittikā).
dhuvati:
dhavati
(and dhuvati1), pr. 3 sg. [S. Dhātup dhravati, dhruvati, Wg §§ 28:107, 22:45], goes; is firm; Dhātum 429 (dhuva yātrāthiresu ca); Sadd 393,.7 (dhu gatitheriyesu: … ~ati dhuvaṃ); — fpp dhavitabba, (mf)n., Sadd 393,.12.

dhunāti
dhuvati2 pr. 3 sg. [S. dhū̆noti, dhuvati], shakes, tosses; shakes off, removes, liberates oneself from; destroys; Dhātup 499 (dhu kampane); Dhātum 720; S I 156,35* (~ātha maccuno senaṃ naḷāgāraṃ va kuñjaro) ≠ Th 1147 (~āma, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se ~āmu; Th-a III 167,.8 : ~āmā ti niddhunāma viddhaṃsema); Sn 682 (~ātha me saṃsayaṃ); Vv 64:9 (~anti vagganti patanti c’ ambare; Vv-a 278,.23 : ~antī ti cāmarabhāraṃ kesarabhāraṃ vāladhiṃ ca vidhunanti, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee wr dhumantī ti); Th 2 (~āti pāpake dhamme dumapattaṃ va māluto); Thī 276 (tīṇi pāpassa mūlāni ~anti sucikārino); Vism 81,.17 (mohaṃ ~āti); Ps II 272,.2 (~eyya); Ap-a 395,.9 (~āti kampatī ti dumo); Sadd 393,.20 (dhū vidhūnane: … dhuvati dhuvitā dhuvitabbaṃ); 497,.7 (dhū kampane: ~āti dhūmo dhonā dhono dhuto); — part.pr. (a) dhuna(t), mfn., Ja IV 371,24* (~aṃ sāmākanīvāraṃ saṅghāriyaṃ pasāriyaṃ); (b) dhunanta, mfn., Ap 273,.20 (~anto vākacīrāni gacchāmi ambare tadā); Sv 268,.14 (mahāvāte thusaṃ ~anto viya, Be, Se so; Ce bhusaṃ opuṇanto; Ee bhusaṃ punanto); Ud-a 167,.1; Nidd-a I 258,.22 (vipannadhammaṃ desanādhammesu ~antesu, Be so; Ce, Ee avipannadhammadesano dhammesu ~antesu; Se vipannadhamme desanadhammesu ~anto); (c) dhunamāna, mfn., Ud 21,12* (sabbakammajahassa bhikkhuno ~amānassa purekataṃ rajaṃ, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se bhūnamānassa); Bv 18:11 (pupphaṃ … paggayha ~amāno upāgamiṃ; Bv-a 230,.21 : vākacīrāni ~amāno va); — aor. 3 sg. (a) adhosi, Sn 787 (adhosi so diṭṭhi-m-idh’ eva sabbaṃ, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee sabbā; Pj II 523,.13 : sabbaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ adhosi pajahi vinodesi); Spk II 313,.27 (samantato adhosi, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee acopi); (b) dhuni, Vism 80,.28 (yo dhutaṅgena attano kilese ~i); Nidd I 83,.4 (adhosi ~i niddhuni pajahi vinodesi …); 3 pl. dhuniṃsu, Ja III 44,.1 (brāhmaṇā hatthe ~iṃsu, Ce, Ee so; Be, Se vidhuniṃsu); — inf. dhunituṃ, Ud-a 204,.6; — absol. dhunitvā, Ja IV 373,6´; Pj II 283,.24 (sāmākā ti ~itvā vā sīsāni uccinitvā vā gayhūpagā tiṇadhaññajāti); — pass. part.pr. dhūyamāna, mfn., Vv-a 174,.29 (vāta-dhutā ti mandena mārutena dhūyamānā, Ce so; Be, Ee, Se dhūpayamānā); —     pp     dhuta,    dhūta,   mfn. and n. [ts; cf AMg dhua, dhuta], 1. (mfn.) shaken, agitated; Abh 744 (dhūto ādhūtacalitā, Be so; Ce ~o); Sadd 497,.7 (dhū kampane … ~o); — ifc see vāta-; — 2. (mfn.) shaken off, removed; abandoned; Nidd I 78,.1 (tāya paññāya kāyaduccaritaṃ ~aṃ ca dhotaṃ ca …; Nidd-a I 206,.12 : kampitaṃ ca dhovitaṃ ca) = 136,.26 (Nidd-a I 258,.27 : ~an ti kattusādhanaṃ ~aṃ paṭhamamaggena dhotaṃ dutiyamaggena); — 3. (mfn.) [cf dhota? Sadd 498,.2 foll. : dhātūnaṃ anekatthatāya dhūdhātu kampanatthe pi dhovanatthe pi vattati], (i) who has shaken off or abandoned (defilements); pure, purified; Vin I 305,.20 (idaṃ bhante naggiyaṃ … ~-tāya pāsādikatāya … saṃvattati, Be so; Ce, Ee ~-ttāya; Se dhūtattāya) ≠ IV 113,.29 (Be ~-ttāya; Ee, Se dhūtattāya; Ce dhutāya); III 21,.13 (appicchassa santuṭṭhassa sallekhassa ~assa pāsādikassa … vaṇṇaṃ bhāsitvā, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se dhūtassa; cf Sp 222,.17 : saṃvaro sallekho ca ~o cā ti vuccati) = IV 213,.23 (Be, Ce so; Se dhūtassa; Ee appicchatāya santuṭṭhiyā sallekhassa dhūtassa pāsādikassa …) ≠ III 171,.14 (Be, Ce, Ee so; Se dhūtassa); III 171,.17 (imāni bhante pañca vatthūni … santuṭṭhiyā sallekhāya ~-tāya pāsādikatāya … saṃvattanti, Be, Ee so; Ce ~āya pāsādikāya; Se dhūtāya pāsādikāya …); 172,.16 (ime kho samaṇā sakyaputtiyā ~ā sallekhavuttino, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se dhūtā; Sp 607,.8 : yā paṭipadā kilese dhunāti tāya samannāgatattā ~ā); Vism 61,.22 (dhutakilesattā ~assa bhikkhuno); — see also dhona; — (ii) which shakes off or removes (defilements); which purifies; Sn 385 (sāvayāmi vo dhammaṃ ~aṃ; Pj II 373,.19 : kilese dhunātī ti ~o, evarūpaṃ kilesadhunanakaṃ paṭipadādhammaṃ); Bv 16:8 (buddho pakāsesi ~e guṇe); Mil 348,1* (ajjhogāḷhe ~e guṇe); Vism 80,.23 (~o ti ~-kileso vā puggalo kilesadhunano vā dhammo); Bv-a 49,.35 (kilese dhunanato ñāṇaṃ ~aṃ nāma); — 4. (n.) [or = dhutaṅga?] shaking off (defilements); an ascetic practice; Th 1120 (nesajjiko hoti sadā ~e rato; Th-a III 156,.12 : sabbakālaṃ ca dhutaguṇe abhirato); — see also avasesadhutāyudha (sv avasesa); — ~’-aṅga, n. (and m.) [dhuta + aṅga2], one of 13 special ascetic practices (undertaken voluntarily, not enjoined upon the saṅgha ); Vin V 193,.16 (~’-aṅgavaggo, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se dhūtaṅga-); Ja I 156,.16 (terasa ~-aṅgāni samādāya); Nidd I 66,.21 (katamaṃ vattaṃ na sīlaṃ, aṭṭha ~’-aṅgāni); Mil 20,.12 (samaṇā sakyaputtiyā pabbajanti ~’-aṅgāni ca pariharanti); 348,4* (bujjheyya ce gihī dhamme ~’-aṅgaṃ nipphalaṃ siyā); Vism 59,.16 (bhagavatā … terasa ~-aṅgāni anuññātāni seyyathīdaṃ paṃsu-kūlikaṅgaṃ tecīvarikaṅgaṃ piṇḍapātikaṅgaṃ sāpadāna-cārikaṅgaṃ ekāsanikaṅgaṃ pattapiṇḍikaṅgaṃ khalu-pacchābhattikaṅgaṃ āraññikaṅgaṃ rukkhamūlikaṅgaṃ abbhokāsikaṅgaṃ sosānikaṅgaṃ yathāsanthatikaṅgaṃ nesajjikaṅgan ti); 61,.21 foll. (sabbān’ eva pan’ etāni tena tena samādānena ~-kilesattā ~assa bhikkhuno aṅgāni kilesadhunanato vā ~an ti laddhavohāraṃ ñāṇaṃ aṅgaṃ etesan ti ~-aṅgāni, atha vā ~āni ca tāni paṭipakkhaniddhunanato aṅgāni ca paṭipattiyā ti pi ~-aṅgāni); Ps I 117,.6 (ahaṃ pi ~’-aṅgaṃ samādiyitvā lābhaṃ uppādemī ti); Dhp-a I 379,.18 (nāpi ’ssa kiñci ~’-aṅgaṃ atthi, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se dhūtaṅgaṃ); Ud-a 201,.24 (sabbe pi ’ssa ~’-aṅgā vuttā ti); Pj II 496,.29 (~’-aṅgaṃ na kuppati); — ~’-aṅgasuddhika, mfn., believing in or seeking purification, release, through the dhutaṅga s; valuing observance of a dhutaṅga above all else; Vism 73,.4 (na ~’-aṅgasuddhikena bhavitabban ti); Sv 836,.36 (~’-aṅgasuddhiko hoti na kammaṭṭhāna-suddhiko, ~’-aṅgam eva arahattaṃ viya sārato pacceti, so read with Be, Ce, Se); — ~’-aṅgika, m (fn)., one who observes dhutaṅga s; Nidd-a I 199,.8; — ~-kilesa, mfn., who has shaken off, destroyed, defilements; Thī 401 (bhikkhuniyo … ~-kilesāyo); Nidd I 78,.27; Vism 61,.21 (~-kilesattā); Pj II 542,.23 (~-kilesena buddhena saddhiṃ); — ~-guṇa, m. [BHS id.], an ascetic practice; Vin III 15,.3 (āyasmā Sudinno evarūpe ~-guṇe samādāya vattati, āraññiko hoti piṇḍapātiko paṃsukūliko sapadānacāriko, Be, Ce so; Ee, Se dhūta-; Sp 206,.28 : kilesaniddhunanake guṇe); Th 1087 (-guṇe visiṭṭho ’haṃ); Ja III 342,.23 (appiccho dhūtaguṇena na tappati, Ee so; Be, Ce, Se ~’-aṅgaguṇena); Bv 1:59 (Mahākassapo … ~-guṇe agganikkhitto, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se dhūta-); Spk I 45,.29; It-a I 7,.22 (terasa ~-guṇā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee ~’-aṅgaguṇā); — ~-dhamma, m. [cf BHS dhutadharma], an ascetic practice; an ascetic quality; Vism 81,.9 (~-dhammā veditabbā ti …); Sv 1,25*; Bv-a 49,.31 (~-guṇo nāma ~-dhammo); Cp-a 315,.20 (terasahi ~-dhammehi); — ~-dhara, mfn. [BHS id.], observing ascetic practices; Ap 375,.13 (āraññakā ~-dharā jhāyino lūkhacīvarā, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee dhūtavādā) = Mil 342,15*; — ~-rata, mfn., devoted to ascetic practices; Ap 26,.17 (āraññakā ~-ratā jhāyino lūkhacīvarā, Be, Ee, Se so; Ce ~-dharā); — ~-va(t), mfn., observing dhutaṅga s; Pj II 494,.24 (~-vā ti maṃ pare jānantū ti); Sadd 393,.21; — ~-vāda, mfn., speaking of, preaching dhutaṅga s; instructing in ascetic practices; S II 156,.2 (bhikkhū ~-vādā); A I 23,.20 (~-vādānaṃ Be, Ce, Ee so; Se dhūta-); Ud 42,.32 (āraddhaviriyo ~-vādo); Mil 380,.20; Vism 80,.29 (yo ~’-aṅgena attano kilese dhuni paraṃ pana ~’-aṅgena na ovadati nānusāsati … ayaṃ ~o na ~-vādo); Nidd-a I 335,.22 (~-vādo ti ~-guṇavādī); — ~-vādaka, mfn., id.; Ap 507,.19 (Kassapaṃ ~-vādakaṃ); — ~-vādi(n), mfn., id.; Ja I 130,.22 (tādisassa … ~-vādissa, Ce, Ee so; Se ~-vādassa; Be mādisassa … ~’-aṅgadharassa) = It-a I 158,.6 (Ce so; Ee ~-vādassa; Be, Se mādisassa … ~-vādissa); — caus. pr. 3 sg. dhāveti2, dhāvayati, Sadd 547,.24 (dhū kampane: dhāveti dhāvayati).
pareta:
1pareta
mfn. [pp of pari√i; S. parīta], 1. encompassed; taken possession of, seized, overcome (by); Ud 33,.13 (puthū avijjāya ~ā bhūtā; Ud-a 214,.19 : avijjāya abhibhūtā); Sn 818 (saṅkappehi ~o so kapaṇo viya jhāyati; Nidd I 149,.26 : phuṭṭho ~o samohito samannāgato pihito); 1123 (manuje pekkhamāno … jarasā ~e); Th 385 (mā sītena ~o vihaññittho); Ja VI 190,3* (sokena ca ~’ asmi Bhūridattaṃ apassatī); Ps I 94,.15 (~ā, phuṭṭhā anugatā ca); — ifc see ghamma-, phassa- (sv phassa1), sneha-; — 2. surrounded; Ap 45,.17 (sabalehi ~o ’haṃ, Be, Ee, Se so; Ce parīto; Ap-a 288,.28 : attano senābalehi ~o parivārito, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee parito); 299,.4 (mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena ~o lokanāyako); 553,.9 (parisāhi ca catūhi ~o lokanāyako, Ee so; Be parivuto; Ce sahito; Se pharate); — see also paricca1.
paridahana:
1paridahana
n. [ts], burning; Ja II 276,10´ (sabbaṅgaparidāhinā ti sabbāni aṅgāni °-samatthena, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se sabbaṅgapariḷāhinā ti); Vism 504,18* (cittassa ca ~ā kāyassa visādanā ca adhimattaṃ yaṃ dukkhaṃ upāyāso janeti); Ud-a 20,.7 (santāpo dukkhadukkhatādivasena santappanaṃ ~aṃ, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee paridahaṇaṃ vā); Paṭis-a 560,.6 (°’-aṭṭhena pariḷāho); As 370,.22 (°’-aṭṭhena kāmapariḷāho, Ee so; Be, Ce pariḍayhanaṭṭhena; Se paridayhanaṭṭhena); — see also pariḍayhana.

2paridahana
n. [from paridahati2], wearing; putting on; As 244,.9 (vatthassa icchiticchitakkhaṇe ~aṃ viya).
paṭibhāsati:
1paṭibhāsati
pr. 3 sg. [S. pratibhāṣate], answers; addresses in return or in reply; Sn 1024 (kam etaṃ ~ati); — aor. 3 sg. (a) paccabhāsi, paṭi-abhāsi, M II 144,.17 (bhagavā Brahmāyuṃ brāhmaṇaṃ gāthāhi paccabhāsi; Ps III 396,.17 foll.: aṭṭhapañhe vyākaronto paṭi-abhāsi); S I 6,.2 (aññatarā devatā taṃ devataṃ gāthāya paccabhāsi); (b) paṭibhāsi2, Mil 20,.29 (āyasmā Āyupālo tuṇhī ahosi na kiñci ~i, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se ~ati); (c) paccabhāsatha, Ja V 349,13*; 1 sg. paccabhāsiṃ, paṭi-abhāsiṃ, Ja V 171,6* (paccabhāsiṃ); Ps II 181,.20 (paṭi-abhāsiṃ); 3 pl. paccabhāsiṃsu, Pv-a 57,.2 (evaṃ sāmaṇerena puṭṭhā te petā … paccabhāsiṃsu, Be, Ce, Ee pacchābhāsiṃsu; Se omits).

2paṭibhāsati
pr. 3 sg. [cf S. pratibhāsate; but perhaps wr for paṭibhāyati influenced by aor. paṭibhāsi1], appears; comes into one’s mind, occurs to one; presents itself to be expressed; Vin IV 177,.24 (ekassa ce pi bhikkhuno na ~eyya taṃ bhikkhuniṃ apasādetuṃ); M I 150,.29 (sace hi mayaṃ jāneyyāmā āyasmā Sāriputto ti ettakaṃ pi no na ~eyya) ≠ A V 198,.12 (Ce, Ee, Se so; Be na ppaṭibhāyeyya); M I 396,.3 (udāhu ṭhānaso v’ etaṃ taṃ ~eyyā ti; cf 395,.29 : udāhu ṭhānaso v’ etaṃ tathāgataṃ paṭibhātī ti); II 31,.6 (tena h’ Udāyi taṃ yev’ ettha paṭibhātu yathā maṃ ~eyyā ti; Ps III 271,.9 foll.: yena kāraṇena mama dhammadesanā upaṭṭhaheyya); III 131,.33 (kuto pana maṃ bhante Jayasenassa rājakumārassa imā dve upamā ~issanti, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be paṭibhāyissanti); S IV 285,.16 (yadā aññadā pi evarūpo pañho āgaccheyya taṃ yev’ ettha ~eyyā ti, Be, Ce, Ee so; Se ~eyyāsī ti); A III 195,.7 (yathā āyasmantaṃ yev’ ettha Upavānaṃ ~eyya; Mp III 299,.9 : āyasmato yeva Upavānassa paṭivacanaṃ paṭibhātu upaṭṭhātū ti); IV 359,.12 (sace hi mayaṃ jāneyyāma bhagavā bahidvārakoṭṭhake ṭhito ti ettakaṃ pi no na ~eyyā ti, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be paṭibhāyeyyā ti; Mp IV 167,.15 foll.: paṭisambhidāpattassa appaṭibhānaṃ nāma natthi, ettakaṃ pana na katheyyan ti dasseti); Ud 27,.13 (sace kho tvaṃ Ānanda jāneyyāsi ettakaṃ pi te na ~eyya, Ce, Ee, Se so; Be paṭibhāyeyya; Ud-a 187,.7 foll.: yadidaṃ te … tikkhattuṃ paṭibhānaṃ upaṭṭhitaṃ ta-y-idaṃ ettakaṃ pi te na upaṭṭhaheyya).
ñatta:
1ñatta
n. [BHS jñātra], skill or accomplishment; a public reputation (for skill or intellectual accomplishment); Dhp 72 (yāvad eva anatthāya ~aṃ bālassa jāyati; Dhp-a II 73,.9 : ~an ti jānanasabhāvo yaṃ pi sippaṃ jānāti yamhi vā issariye yase sampattiyaṃ ca ṭhito janena ñāyati pākaṭo paññāto hoti tass’ etaṃ nāmaṃ); Ps II 384,.11; Sadd 350,.27 (ñā avabodhane: … ~aṃ); 351,.4 (~an ti jānanabhāvo); —    °’-ajjhāpanna,    mfn., who has obtained a good reputation; M I 318,.29 (ñattajjhāpanno ayaṃ āyasmā bhikkhu yasaṃ patto saṃvijjant’ assa idh’ ekacce ādīnavā ti; Ps II 384,.11 foll. : ñattaṃ paññāta-bhāvaṃ pākatabhāvaṃ ajjhāpanno nu kho).
adhiccasamuppattika:
2adhicca
mfn. and ind. [perhaps = adhicca1], 1. (mfn.) fortuitous, occurring by mere chance; rare; S V 457,.3 (~aṃ idaṃ bhante yaṃ so kāṇo kacchapo … amusmiṃ ekacchiggaḷe yuge gīvaṃ paveseyyā ti evaṃ ~aṃ idaṃ bhikkhave yaṃ manussattaṃ labhati; Spk III 302,.10 : idaṃ adhiccuppattikaṃ); — adhiccena, adv., without cause; rarely; Ap-a 488,.9 (~ena akāraṇena); — 2. (ind.) fortuitously, without cause or reason; rarely; only iic; —      °’-āpattika,   mfn., rarely or occasionally offending; Vin V 115,.19 (~o puggalo); M I 443,.22 (ekacco bhikkhu ~o hoti anāpattibahulo; Ps III 154,.16 : ~o ti kadāci kadāci āpattiṃ āpajjati); —       °’-uppatti,   f., occasional appearance; As 238,.30 (~iyā); —       °’-uppattika,   mfn., appearing without a cause; rarely appearing; Ap 302,.8 (ayaṃ ca buddho uppanno ~o muni); 419,.22 (~ā buddhā; Ap-a 488,.9 : adhiccena akāraṇena uppattikā sayambhūtā); —       °-laddha,   mfn., obtained by chance, without a cause; Vv 84:22 (~aṃ pariṇāmajaṃ te sayaṃkataṃ udāhu devehi dinnaṃ; Vv-a 341,.16 : ~an ti adhiccasamuppattikaṃ yadicchakaṃ laddhan ti attho) ≠ Ja V 171,9* ( 171,18´ : ~an ti ahetunā laddhaṃ); —       °-samuppattika,   mfn., appearing without a cause, fortuitously; Vv-a 341,.16; —       °-samuppanna,   mfn., arisen fortuitously, without cause or reason; connected with fortuitous or causeless origination; D I 28,.21 (~aṃ attānaṃ ca lokaṃ ca paññāpenti; Sv 118,.7 : ~an ti akāraṇasamuppannaṃ); III 33,.15 (~aṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññāpenti); S II 22,.25 (kiṃ … ~aṃ sukhadukkhan ti) ≠ Vibh 377,.3; Vism 209,.28 foll. (catubbidhaṃ vā nāmaṃ āvatthikaṃ … ~an ti, ~aṃ nāma lokiyavohārena yadicchakan ti vuttaṃ hoti … vacanatthaṃ anapekkhitvā pavattam ~aṃ); Sv 118,.5 foll. (~o attā ca loko cā ti dassanaṃ ~aṃ); —       °-samuppannika,   mfn., (one) who believes in fortuitous or causeless origination; D I 28,.20 (eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ~ā); Ps I 70,.29 (~ass’ eva sassatadiṭṭhi) ≠ Paṭis-a 419,.13.
adhiccāpattika:

dhammasavanagga:
1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll. (ahaṃ kho āvuso navo acirappabbajito adhunāgato imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ na t’ ahaṃ sakkomi vitthārena ~aṃ desituṃ api ca te saṅkhittena atthaṃ vakkhāmī ti … ye ~ā hetuppabhavā tesaṃ hetuṃ tathāgato āha tesaṃ ca yo nirodho evaṃvādī mahāsamaṇo; Sp 975,.19 : ye ~ā hetuppabhavā ti hetuppabhavā nāma pañcakkhandhā); III 1,.18 (iti pi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho … so imaṃ lokaṃ … sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti so ~aṃ deseti ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhe kalyāṇaṃ pariyosāna-kalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ savyañjanaṃ …); D I 62,.24 foll. (tathāgato loke uppajjati … so ~aṃ deseti … taṃ ~aṃ suṇāti gahapati … taṃ ~aṃ sutvā tathāgate saddhaṃ paṭilabhati … so aparena samayena … agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati); II 55,.14 (etassa Ānanda ~assa ananubodhā appaṭivedhā evaṃ ayaṃ pajā tantākulakajātā … apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ saṃsāraṃ nātivattati); 1dhamma
m. (and n.) [S., BHS dharma], dhamma denotes (an interpretation of) the essential nature and reality of existence and experience, the way things are: it is descriptive and prescriptive; it denotes also an essential attribute of men or animals; a quality or characteristic; Abh 784 (~o sabhāve pariyattipaññāñāyesu saccappakatīsu puññe ñeyye guṇācārasamādhisū pi nissattatāpattisu kāraṇādo); see also Sv 99,.3 foll., Ps I 17,.16 foll., It-a I 37,.20 foll., Paṭis-a 18,.1 foll., Bv-a 13,.4 foll., As 38,.23 foll. and Sadd 560,.25 foll.; — for Buddhists dhamma is used to denote an interlocking and interdependent assembly of concepts: the true nature of the world of experience, how that world works, and the way to transcend it, as understood by the Buddha; the progressive stages of understanding and nibbāna ; the behaviour, the practice, required to achieve understanding of the way the world of experience works, ie the way to reach arhatship, nibbāna ; the understanding and practice taught by the Buddha, the substance of his teaching, the texts of the Canon, especially the Suttapiṭaka ; all constituents of the world of experience, physical and mental, external and internal, progressively more and more minutely analysed; all constituents of prescribed practice, appropriate and beneficial actions; prescriptions for the members of the saṅgha ; — for people generally dhamma is an interpretation of the essential nature of existence and experience; the way one should act, depending on who one is, to maintain the way things are and should be; duty; right; justice; normative and beneficial actions; — 1. (i) how the world of experience works, the processes by which it works and is explained (especially as formulated in cattāri ariyasaccāni and paṭiccasamuppāda ), and the possibility and way of transcending it, as understood by the Buddha and taught by him (so that knowledge and understanding of it might bring enlightenment, arhatship, to others); Vin I 2,3* (yadā have pātubhavanti ~ā ātāpino jhāyato brāhmaṇassa ath’ assa kaṅkhā vapayanti sabbā yato pajānāti sahetudhammaṃ; Sp 954,.19 foll. : pātubhavantī ti uppajjanti ~ā ti anulomapaccayākārapaṭivedhasādhakā bodhipakkhiyadhammā, atha vā pātubhavantī ti pakāsenti abhisamayavasena vyattā pākaṭā honti, ~ā ti caturāriyasaccadhammā); 11,.2 (idaṃ dukkhaṃ ariyasaccan ti me bhikkhave pubbe ananussutesu ~esu cakkhuṃ udapādi); 12,.24 (ehi bhikkhū ti bhagavā avoca svākkhāto ~o cara brahmacariyaṃ sammā dukkhassa antakiriyāyā ti); 15,.31 (idaṃ kho Yasa anupaddutaṃ idaṃ anupassaṭṭhaṃ ehi Yasa nisīda ~aṃ te desessāmī ti); 40,.19 foll.
